117	def exclusion(comp):
118	    """Why RDT's entry is not a component, from what RDT reports about it, or None. RDT lists every function it can
119	    give a parameter to, so hooks, route handlers, helpers and context objects come with it. The evidence is the shape:
120	    props that are the members of a TypeScript lib type (`String`, `Function`, `Request`) mean the parameter is not an
121	    object of props; a hook is named `use` and a capital; a `value` declared by `@types/react` and nothing else is a
122	    context's Provider; a lowercase name cannot be a JSX tag unless it takes the attributes of one (a `@types/react`
123	    prop) or is the file's or directory's own name, which RDT gives a default export; and props that are all promises
124	    are handed over by a router, not by a parent."""
125	    props = comp['props']
126	    in_lib = sum(bool(LIB_FILE.search(i.get('parent') or '')) for i in props.values())
127	    if in_lib * 2 > len(props):
128	        return 'lib_members'
129	    name = comp['name']
130	    if re.match(r'use[A-Z0-9]', name):
131	        return 'hook'
132	    if 'value' in props and set(props) <= {'value', 'children'} and all(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
133	        return 'context_value'
134	    path = comp['file']
135	    own_names = {norm_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]), norm_name(os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path)))}
136	    if name[:1].islower() and norm_name(name) not in own_names and not any(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
137	        return 'not_jsx'
138	    if all(i.get('type', '').startswith('Promise<') for i in props.values()):
139	        return 'promise_props'
140	    return None

143	def read_text(path):
144	    """A source file's text, or None if there is no such file."""

151	def import_binding(text, name):
152	    """Where `name` was imported from in `text`: (module, imported name) or None."""
153	    for match in re.finditer(r"^import\s+(?:type\s+)?([^;'\"]*?)\s+from\s+['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text, re.M):
154	        clause, module = match.groups()
155	        if not clause.startswith('{'):
156	            default, _, clause = clause.partition(',')
157	            if default.strip() == name:
158	                return module, 'default'
159	        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', clause.partition('{')[2].partition('}')[0]):
160	            if (alias or original) == name:
161	                return module, original
162	    return None

165	def export_source(text, name):
166	    """How `text` exports `name` (`default` or a name): ('local', local name), ('from', module, name) or None."""
167	    if name == 'default':
168	        # The second pattern unwraps calls whose first argument is an identifier (`memo(Foo)`, `observer(forwardRef(Foo))`):
169	        # the wrapper is whatever function the file calls, so the name that matters is the innermost identifier.
170	        for pattern in (r'^export\s+default\s+(?:async\s+)?(?:function\*?|class)\s+(\w+)',
171	                        r'^export\s+default\s+(?:\w+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(\s*)*(\w+)(?=\s*(?:[,);]|$))'):
172	            match = re.search(pattern, text, re.M)
173	            if match:
174	                return 'local', match.group(1)
175	    else:
176	        declaration = rf'^export\s+(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function\*?|class|async\s+function)\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'
177	        if re.search(declaration, text, re.M):
178	            return 'local', name
179	    for match in re.finditer(r"^export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*(?:from\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"])?", text, re.M):
180	        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', match.group(1)):
181	            if (alias or original) == name:
182	                return ('from', match.group(2), original) if match.group(2) else ('local', original)
183	    return None

186	def resolve_module(file, module, exists):
187	    """The file `module` names from `file` (relative paths only), as a path relative to the root."""
188	    if not module.startswith('.'):
189	        return None
190	    base = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(file), module))
191	    return next((base + ext for ext in EXTENSIONS if exists(base + ext)), None)

194	def export_target(file, read, exists, name='default', hops=6):
195	    """The file and local name where what `file` exports as `name` is defined: follows `export default X`,
196	    `import X from`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }` through re-exports. None where it ends elsewhere."""
197	    text = read(file)
198	    exported = export_source(text, name) if text and hops else None
199	    if not exported:
200	        return None
201	    if exported[0] == 'from':
202	        target = resolve_module(file, exported[1], exists)
203	        return export_target(target, read, exists, exported[2], hops - 1) if target else None
204	    imported = import_binding(text, exported[1])
205	    if imported:
206	        target = resolve_module(file, imported[0], exists)
207	        return export_target(target, read, exists, imported[1], hops - 1) if target else None
208	    return file, exported[1]

211	def counterpart(file, name, found_by_file):
212	    """Caliper's key in `file` for a component called `name`, or None: the names must agree, since a file's only
213	    component says nothing about whether RDT's entry is that component."""
214	    return (file, norm_name(name)) if norm_name(name) in found_by_file.get(file, {}) else None

217	def pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists):
218	    """Caliper's key and the evidence for RDT's entry that Caliper reports in another file: where the default export of
219	    RDT's file is defined (RDT names a default export after the file or directory) or, for a named export, where that is,
220	    else the file that declares its props, when Caliper reports a component of that name there. None if neither leads to one."""
221	    file = relative(comp['file'], root)
222	    for export in ('default', comp['name']):
223	        target = export_target(file, read, exists, export)
224	        found = counterpart(target[0], target[1], found_by_file) if target and target[0] != file else None
225	        if found:
226	            return found, 'default_export' if export == 'default' else 'named_export'
227	    name = norm_name(comp['name'])
228	    for info in comp['props'].values():
229	        parent = info.get('parent') or ''
230	        declared = relative(parent, root) if parent and REACT_DIR not in parent else None
231	        if declared and declared != file and name in found_by_file.get(declared, {}):
232	            return (declared, name), 'declaration'
233	    return None

236	def reference(rdt_components, found, root):
237	    """The components recall is measured on, from RDT's output: entries with props, minus those that are not components
238	    (`exclusion`), with every RDT entry for one component counted once. An entry that Caliper reports under another file
239	    pairs with it by evidence (`pair`) and joins the entry in that file; RDT's repeats of one key join too. Each item is
240	    {'keys': every (file, name) a tool may report it under, 'props': prop -> 'own' | 'react'}, so one list serves every
241	    tool. Also the counts, so a change in the reference shows in weekly.json."""
242	    found_by_file = {}
243	    for file, name in found:
244	        found_by_file.setdefault(file, {})[name] = None
245	    exists = lambda rel: os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, rel))
246	    read = lambda rel: read_text(os.path.join(root, rel))
247	    stats = {'rdt_with_props': 0, 'excluded': {}, 'exact': 0, 'paired': {}, 'merged': 0}
248	    groups = {}
249	    for comp in rdt_components:
250	        if not comp['props']:
251	            continue
252	        stats['rdt_with_props'] += 1
253	        why = exclusion(comp)
254	        if why:
255	            stats['excluded'][why] = stats['excluded'].get(why, 0) + 1
256	            continue
257	        key = (relative(comp['file'], root), norm_name(comp['name']))
258	        target = key if key in found else None
259	        if target:
260	            stats['exact'] += 1
261	        else:
262	            paired = pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists)
263	            if paired:
264	                target = paired[0]
265	                stats['paired'][paired[1]] = stats['paired'].get(paired[1], 0) + 1
266	        keys = [key] + ([target] if target else [])
267	        group = groups.get(target or key)
268	        if group is None:
269	            group = groups[target or key] = {'keys': [], 'exact': {}, 'other': {}}
270	        else:
271	            stats['merged'] += 1
272	        group['keys'] += keys
273	        # The props of the entries in the component's own file when there are any, else of all the repeats united, so the
274	        # reference does not depend on the order RDT lists them in. A prop any repeat takes from `@types/react` is one.
275	        into = group['exact' if key == target else 'other']
276	        for prop, info in comp['props'].items():
277	            into[prop] = 'react' if into.get(prop) == 'react' or declared_in_react(info) else 'own'
278	    items = [{'keys': list(dict.fromkeys(g['keys'])), 'props': g['exact'] or g['other']} for g in groups.values()]
279	    stats['reference'] = len(items)
280	    stats['unpaired'] = sum(not any(k in found for k in item['keys']) for item in items)
281	    stats['excluded_total'] = sum(stats['excluded'].values())
282	    return items, stats

285	def recall(items, found, layered=None):
286	    """Against the reference: the components the tool also reports and, of those, RDT's props it lists, apart from and
287	    with `@types/react`'s, so a missing component and a missing prop are counted once each. `own` and `react` count the
288	    props listed as props; `own_layers` and `react_layers` also count those held in a collapsed layer (`layered`), which
289	    the output names without listing them."""
290	    layered = layered or {}
291	    count = {'components': [0, 0], 'own': [0, 0], 'react': [0, 0], 'own_layers': [0, 0], 'react_layers': [0, 0]}
292	    for item in items:
293	        count['components'][1] += 1
294	        key = next((k for k in item['keys'] if k in found), None)
295	        if key is None:
296	            continue
297	        in_layers = layered.get(key, set())
298	        count['components'][0] += 1
299	        for prop, kind in item['props'].items():
300	            count[kind][1] += 1
301	            count[kind][0] += prop in found[key]
302	            count[f'{kind}_layers'][1] += 1
303	            count[f'{kind}_layers'][0] += prop in found[key] or prop in in_layers
304	    return count

307	def rate(pair):
308	    return pair[0] / pair[1] if pair[1] else 0.0

311	def oracle(binary, name, src, root, work):
312	    """How often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types (apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts)."""
313	    caliper_json = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.caliper.json')
314	    with open(caliper_json, 'w') as f:
315	        subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
316	                        '--load-dependencies', '--quiet'], stdout=f, check=True)
317	    list_file, tsconfig = program_inputs(name, src, work)
318	    verdicts = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.oracle.json')
319	    subprocess.run(['pnpm', '--dir', os.path.join(ROOT, 'apps', 'oracle'), 'exec', 'tsx', 'src/oracle.ts', '--root', root,
320	                    '--src', src, '--tsconfig', tsconfig, '--caliper', caliper_json, '--out', verdicts, '--files',
321	                    list_file], check=True, timeout=3600)
322	    with open(verdicts) as f:
323	        e = json.load(f)
324	    shared = e['props_shared']
325	    return {'shared_props': shared, 'agree': rate((e['verdicts']['identical'] + e['verdicts']['spelled'], shared)),
326	            'wrong': rate((e['verdicts']['wrong'], shared))}

336	    rdt_out = os.path.join(work, f"{corpus['name']}.rdt.json")
337	    rdt, rdt_components = tool_run(['node', '--max-old-space-size=8192', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdt.mjs'),

339	    print(f"{corpus['name']}: react-docgen", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

341	    rdg, rdg_components = tool_run(['node', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdg.mjs'), list_file, rdg_out], rdg_out)
342	    print(f"{corpus['name']}: Caliper", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

344	    caliper_found = caliper_components(args.bin, src, root)

346	    entry = {

349	        'rdt': rdt,

352	        'recall': {'caliper': recall(items, caliper_found, caliper_layer_members(args.bin, src, root)),
353	                   'react_docgen': recall(items, found)},
354	    }

363	def findings(record, previous):
364	    """What got worse since `previous`: Caliper's time and memory by more than 10%, its recall by more than 2 points."""
365	    out = []
366	    for name, entry in record['corpora'].items():
367	        old = previous.get('corpora', {}).get(name)
368	        if not old:
369	            continue
370	        for key, label in (('ms', 'time'), ('rss_mib', 'peak memory')):
371	            if entry['caliper'][key] > SLOWER * old['caliper'][key]:
372	                out.append(f"{name}: {label} {old['caliper'][key]} -> {entry['caliper'][key]}")
373	        for kind in ('components', 'own', 'react', 'own_layers', 'react_layers'):
374	            if kind not in old['recall']['caliper']:
375	                continue  # a record from before layers were counted
376	            now, before = rate(entry['recall']['caliper'][kind]), rate(old['recall']['caliper'][kind])
377	            if now < before - RECALL_DROP:
378	                out.append(f'{name}: recall of {kind} {100 * before:.1f}% -> {100 * now:.1f}%')
379	    return out

382	def markdown(record, notes):
383	    lines = [f"Caliper {record['caliper']}, median of {record['runs']} runs; RDT and react-docgen one run each. Whole "
384	             'process, Node start included.', '', '### Time and memory', '',
385	             '| Corpus | Caliper | JSON | RDT | react-docgen |', '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
386	    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
387	        cell = lambda t: f"{t['ms'] / 1000:.2f} s, {t['rss_mib']:,} MiB"
388	        lines.append(f"| {name} | {cell(e['caliper'])} | {e['caliper']['json_mb']} MB | {cell(e['rdt'])} | "
389	                     f"{cell(e['react_docgen'])} |")
390	    lines += ['', '### Reference (RDT, cleaned)', '',
391	              '| Corpus | RDT entries with props | Not components | Repeats merged | Reference | Same file | Paired | Unpaired |',
392	              '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
393	    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
394	        r = e['reference']
395	        lines.append(f"| {name} | {r['rdt_with_props']} | {r['excluded_total']} | {r['merged']} | {r['reference']} | "
396	                     f"{r['exact']} | {sum(r['paired'].values())} | {r['unpaired']} |")
397	    lines += ['', '### Recall against the reference', '',
398	              '| Corpus | Tool | Components | Own props | Own, with layers | `@types/react` props | `@types/react`, with layers |',
399	              '| --- | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
400	    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
401	        for tool in ('caliper', 'react_docgen'):
402	            r = e['recall'][tool]
403	            # A tool that writes no layers (react-docgen) has the same count with and without them.
404	            kinds = ('components', 'own', 'own_layers', 'react', 'react_layers')
405	            lines.append(f'| {name} | {tool} | ' + ' | '.join(f'{100 * rate(r.get(k, r[k.removesuffix("_layers")])):.1f}%'
406	                                                              for k in kinds) + ' |')
407	    oracle_rows = [(n, e['oracle']) for n, e in record['corpora'].items() if 'oracle' in e]
408	    if oracle_rows:
409	        lines += ['', "### TypeScript 7.1's checker (information)", '', '| Corpus | Shared props | Agree | Wrong |',
410	                  '| --- | --: | --: | --: |']
411	        for name, o in oracle_rows:
412	            lines.append(f'| {name} | unavailable: {o["error"][:80]} | | |' if 'error' in o else
413	                         f"| {name} | {o['shared_props']:,} | {100 * o['agree']:.1f}% | {100 * o['wrong']:.2f}% |")
414	    if notes:
415	        lines += ['', '### Worse than last week', ''] + [f'- {n}' for n in notes]
416	    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

420	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
421	    parser.add_argument('--bin', required=True)

423	    parser.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[])

437	    notes = []

def prop(parent=''):

class Tree(unittest.TestCase):
    FILES = {}

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.root = os.path.realpath(self.dir.name)
        for rel, text in self.FILES.items():
            path = os.path.join(self.root, rel)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
            with open(path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(text)

    def entry(self, name, rel, props):
        return {'name': name, 'file': os.path.join(self.root, rel), 'props': props}


class PairsOnlyByName(Tree):
    FILES = {'a.tsx': 'const Helper = () => null;\nexport default Helper;\n', 'index.tsx': 'export { default } from "./a";\n'}

    def test_default_export_of_another_name_does_not_pair(self):
        # RDT's `index` entry resolves to the local Helper in a.tsx; Caliper reports only `other` there.
        found = {('a.tsx', 'other'): {'x'}}
        items, stats = weekly.reference([self.entry('index', 'index.tsx', {'x': prop()})], found, self.root)
        self.assertEqual(stats['paired'], {})
        self.assertEqual(stats['unpaired'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(weekly.recall(items, found)['components'], [0, 1])

    def test_default_export_of_the_same_name_pairs(self):
        found = {('a.tsx', 'helper'): {'x'}}
        items, stats = weekly.reference([self.entry('index', 'index.tsx', {'x': prop()})], found, self.root)
        self.assertEqual(stats['paired'], {'default_export': 1})
        self.assertEqual(items[0]['keys'], [('index.tsx', 'index'), ('a.tsx', 'helper')])

# Measurement

Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.

## Weekly record

`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and `.d.ts` files from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.

| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |

It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies`; its time is the median of five runs. RDT and react-docgen run once each.

Each run's peak RSS is that process's own. `scripts/corpora.py` starts every measured command through a small helper that forks it and reads its `wait4` usage. Reading it straight from the weekly script gave one number for every run after the largest: on Linux a child's `ru_maxrss` starts at the highest RSS its parent ever had, and the script's own peak (it holds RDT's output for a large corpus) became every later tool's "peak". The first weekly record shows 1,593 MiB for all three tools on shadcn, antd and spectrum, which is that. `scripts/test_weekly.py` checks that a large parent no longer leaks in.

### The reference

Recall is measured against RDT's output, cleaned in two steps. Both are by what RDT reports, never by library or name lists, and `weekly.json` keeps their counts (`reference` per corpus) so a change in either is visible.

| Step | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Not components, left out | More than half of the props are declared in TypeScript's own `lib.*.d.ts` (the parameter is a `string`, a `Request`, a function: `GET`, `loadHighlighter`, `convertLegacyProps`). The name is a hook's (`use` and a capital). The only props are a `value` (and `children`) declared by `@types/react`, which is a context's Provider (`FormContext`). The name starts lowercase, is not the file's or directory's name (RDT names a default export after those) and no prop comes from `@types/react`, so it is no JSX tag and takes no tag's attributes (`genLinkStyle`, `generateMetadata`). Every prop is a `Promise<...>`, which a router hands over (`page`). |
| Repeats, counted once | RDT lists one component under each file that re-exports it, and names a default export after the file or directory (antd's `col/index.tsx` default-exports `Col` from `../grid` and RDT reports `col` there; Caliper reports the defining file). An entry that Caliper does not report in its own file pairs by evidence: where the default export, or the named export, of RDT's file is defined (followed through `export default X`, `import`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }`), or else the file that declares its props when Caliper reports a component of that name there. Entries that pair with the same Caliper component are one reference item. |

The record shows, per corpus: RDT's entries with props, how many are not components, how many repeats were merged, the reference size, how many match in the same file, how many are paired (by default export, named export or declaration) and how many stay unpaired. Pairing needs the names to agree: the component the export resolves to must have the name Caliper reports, so an entry never pairs with an unrelated component just because it is the only one in its file. When several RDT entries pair to one component, the reference takes the props of the entry in the component's own file, else the union of the repeats'. An unpaired item is a component Caliper does not report where RDT does, and it stays in the denominator.

The 2026-10-31 effect on the pinned corpora, Caliper's component recall (own and `@types/react` props are unchanged by the exclusions and move only a little with the pairing):

| Corpus | Reference before |                                           After | Components before | After |
| ------ | ---------------: | ----------------------------------------------: | ----------------: | ----: |
| shadcn |             1594 |                   1573 (21 left out, 0 repeats) |             95.2% | 96.5% |
| antd   |              258 | 203 (43 left out, 12 repeats merged, 12 paired) |             64.0% | 81.3% |

Exclusions alone give 76.7% on antd, pairing alone 68.3%. shadcn has no re-export of this kind in the pinned commit, so nothing pairs there; its unpaired items are `Icons.logo`-style object members, aliases such as `const ComboboxRoot = Primitive.Root` and factory results, which Caliper does not detect.

Recall is measured against that reference, on the components both tools report (same file, same name, or paired):

| Measure              | Meaning                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Components           | The reference's components that the tool also reports                                     |
| Own props            | Of those components, RDT's props not declared by `@types/react` that the tool lists       |
| `@types/react` props | RDT's props that `@types/react` declares (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `ref`) that the tool lists |
| ... with layers      | The same two, also counting a prop held in a collapsed inheritance layer                  |

Caliper collapses an inherited dependency source of more than 30 props into a layer (ADR 0012) and lists only its notable members as props, as Storybook does. A prop in a layer is in the output, named by the layer's `members`, but is not in the flat list, so the table reports both: the plain columns say what the default output lists, "with layers" says what it holds. react-docgen writes no layers, so its two columns are equal.

react-docgen reads each file alone with its default resolver and importer, as Storybook does, so it lists no types declared elsewhere. That is the point of the comparison.

The run uploads `weekly.json` and a table to the job summary. It compares with the last successful run's `weekly.json` and opens, or comments on, one issue labelled `weekly-measurement` when Caliper's time or memory is more than 10% worse, or its recall is more than 2 points lower, on any corpus. There is no committed baseline: the previous run is the baseline.

### TypeScript's checker as the oracle

RDT has mistakes of its own. With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript/sync` of `7.1.0-beta`) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`. The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts. This is information only: the checker is a beta and the backend that uses it is an opt-in (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).

| Verdict           | Meaning                                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identical         | Both sides describe the same type                                                |
| Spelled           | The same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it                      |
| Less precise      | Caliper's type is looser or left unevaluated                                     |
| Wrong             | Caliper's type describes something else, such as a literal union missing members |
| Checker any/error | The checker has no type                                                          |

## `just bench`

```bash
just bench                 # this checkout, uncommitted work included, against origin/main
just bench my-branch       # a branch
```

`scripts/bench.py` builds both in release mode, then times `extract --json` over Mantine and Chakra (source directory only, nothing installed, dependency loading off, no cache) with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first. It prints the median wall time and peak RSS of each and their ratio. The first run fetches the two source directories into `.corpora/`.

With nothing changed, the ratio stays inside 1.04 for time (95th percentile, 100 trials per corpus on CI and a laptop) and inside 1.12 for memory on CI runners. More than 1.10× in time or 1.20× in memory is worth looking at. Nothing enforces that. Run it before a resolver change goes up for review, and say in the pull request when a cost is intended.

## What this replaces

Before the weekly record, four workflows (Equivalence, Parity, Scorecard and Allow-list empty) ran against every pull request or `main` push, backed by `scripts/equivalence.py`, a per-pull-request allow-list directory and two committed baselines. They caught one regression in speed and one in output that review would have missed. They also failed on runner noise, on bases that had moved and on their own allow-list, and a lot of one week of merge work went to keeping them green. Git history has them.

What we give up: a pull request that slows the resolver or changes output no longer fails by itself. Review, `just bench` and the weekly issue catch it, the last one days later.

input.topic: Weekly harness pairing and exclusion: replay on shadcn and antd, with an over-pairing check
input.headline: Replaying the new rules reproduces the baseline exactly: antd 165/207 and shadcn 1518/1573. Adding the rules gives antd 186/195 (95.4%) with strict identity wrappers, or 186/194 (95.9%) keeping today's any-call unwrap. A key-collision fix adds one more component (187). shadcn does not move, because none of its 55 unmatched entries is a pairing case; they are real Caliper gaps (aliases of external components, object members, factory results). Two guards stop over-pairing: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own name, and a Caliper key an exact RDT entry already claims in the same file cannot be a pairing target. Without them 5 wrong pairs appear and antd reads 188/192 (97.9%). Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum are not replayable locally; validate them from the CI weekly artifact on a branch run.

findings.claim: Baseline reproduces: antd exact 165, paired default_export 6 and named_export 2, merged 8, reference 207, matched 165/207 (79.7%). shadcn exact 1518, reference 1573, matched 1518/1573 (96.5%). dl-new weekly.json (run 41479003541, main 53970b80) has the same reference counts for both. Mantine 328/368, Chakra 614/664 and Spectrum 998/1023 come from that file only. docs/measurement.md says antd 81.3% on 203 items, which is stale against the run.
findings.evidence: Ran scratch/base.py against the earlier agent's RDT dumps (agent-a72ef.../scratch/w/*.rdt.json) and a fresh 'cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen' on origin/main 53970b80; compared to dl-new/weekly/weekly.json.

findings.claim: Class A1/A2, same-file and cross-file default export. Pair when (1) the RDT name equals the own name of its file (basename, or directory for index.*), which is the name RDT gives a default export, and (2) the file's default export resolves, through the local-alias chain, to an identifier that Caliper reports in the same file or in the file the chain ends in. Today pair() ignores any target in RDT's own file (weekly.py:224 'target[0] != file') and export_source cannot read 'X as T', 'Object.assign(X, ...)' or 'React.memo(X)' (weekly.py:170-171). Effect on antd: 26 new pairs, of which 21 become new matches (skeleton x5, Addon, Number, Timer, FilterWrapper, panelRender, Section, iconUtil, Ellipsis, checkbox/Group, ColorSlider, PreviewGroup, image/Progress, locale, menu, radio/group, dropdown) and 5 are repeats merged into a component already counted (collapse, masonry, radio, statistic, table). The 8 existing pairs are unchanged.
findings.evidence: scratch/weekly2.py, 'SPLIT' listing: 13 merges (8 old plus 5 new) and 21 NEWMATCH. 186 = 165 + 21. Matched props: own 2963/3426 vs 2731/3162, @types/react 10995/11098 vs 10276/10373.

findings.claim: Resolver design (replayed). local(file, L): (a) try L and the literal of 'L.displayName = "X"' as Caliper names in the file (image/Progress -> 'ImageProgress'); (b) if L is imported, follow default or named export through resolve_module, or end 'external' for a non-relative module; (c) if 'const L = expr', unwrap expr (strip ' as T', ' satisfies T', parens, '!'; unwrap Object.assign / memo / forwardRef / observer and, as today, any call whose first argument is an identifier; dotted callees such as React.memo) and recurse; a call with no identifier argument ends 'factory'; a member expression ends 'external' or 'member'; (d) a function or class declaration ends 'declared'. Hop limit 8. Handled antd shapes: 'CheckboxGroup as <T>(...)', 'Object.assign(Collapse, {...})', 'React.memo(RadioGroup)', 'const Table = forwardRef(Inner) as ...', 'const Dropdown = InternalDropdown as typeof ... & {...}', 'export default Statistic as CompoundedStatistic'.
findings.evidence: scratch/weekly2.py Resolver.local/export, unwrap(), default_expr(); statement() cuts at a depth-0 ';' or newline.

findings.claim: Class A5/A6 exclusion by shape removes 7 antd entries and no entry Caliper reports. 'not_jsx_default' (6): the RDT name is the file's own name and starts lowercase, the file's default export resolves to a lowercase identifier, and no prop comes from @types/react. It hits confirm, dropIndicator and the four generate* factories (generateCalendar, generateRangePicker, generateSinglePicker, generatePicker), which return components rather than being one. 'static_member' (1): a dotted RDT name whose assignment 'Owner.prop = value' has a lowercase identifier value (ConfigProvider.config = setGlobalConfig). Excluded entries that Caliper reports: 0 in antd and shadcn. A JSX-text check would not work for confirm.tsx, because it contains JSX inside render(<...>).
findings.evidence: scratch/exl.py lists every entry hit by a new exclusion on both corpora, none flagged CALIPER-HAS-IT. Counts: antd lib_members 12, hook 10, not_jsx 12, context_value 9 (old) plus the 7 new, 50 excluded in total.

findings.claim: Do NOT exclude 'RefIcon' or any 'name not in file text' entry. The shape also matches 4 shadcn entries that are real aliases Caliper misses (ComboboxRoot x3, SelectRoot, from 'const Combobox = ComboboxPrimitive.Root'). RefIcon is the value of 'export const IconMap = {success: CheckCircleFilled, ...}' in result/index.tsx, which RDT names after the imported icon. Keep it in the denominator with cause 'name_not_in_file'. If you still want it out, a rule that tells it from ComboboxRoot would need the exported object-of-imports shape, and that is 1 of 195.
findings.evidence: A first replay with the rule as an exclusion removed RefIcon plus 4 shadcn entries; scratch/pk.py shows result/index.tsx:19-23 and no 'RefIcon' word in the file. shadcn reference would have fallen 1573 to 1569 with no change in matches, a harness-made rise.

findings.claim: Splitter/Panel.tsx: Caliper reports two components under the key (file,'panel'): the InternalPanel with displayName 'Panel' (12 props) and the real Panel (9 props). caliper_components (weekly.py:86-87) keeps the last, so BOTH RDT entries are compared with the 9-prop one. This is the only collision in antd (251 Caliper entries, 250 keys) and shadcn has none (1891/1891). The one-to-one guard leaves InternalPanel unmatched with cause key_collision. A fix: give repeated keys a '#2' suffix in caliper_components and caliper_layer_members, and assign RDT entries to the colliding Caliper entries by best prop overlap. Measured overlap: InternalPanel vs the 12-prop entry 12/13 (0.92) against 9/13 (0.69) for the other; Panel vs the 9-prop entry 1.0. That adds one match (187).
findings.evidence: scratch/ov.py and scratch/coll.py; RDT Panel.tsx entries InternalPanel 13 props and Panel 9 props.

findings.claim: Over-pairing checks, each tested on the data. (1) Own-name guard: the default-export route runs only when norm(RDT name) is in the file's own names. Off, antd goes to 188/195 (2 spurious matches). (2) Same-file claim guard: a pairing target in RDT's own file cannot be a key that an exact RDT entry there already claims. Off, InternalPanel merges into Panel (186/194). (3) Name agreement: the end of the chain must be an identifier (or its displayName literal) that Caliper reports in the target file, never the sole component in the file. (4) One chain, no fallback to the declaring file for same-file cases. (5) Hop limit and cycle bound. (6) Collision keys are not paired. With guards (1) and (2) both off, 5 wrong pairs appear: Form.List -> Form, Mentions.Option -> Mentions, RefIcon -> Result, InternalPanel -> Panel, Tour._InternalPanel... -> Tour, giving 188/192 = 97.9%, against 186/195 = 95.4% with them on.
findings.evidence: NO_OWN=1 and NO_CLAIM=1 switches in scratch/weekly2.py; scratch/guard.txt vs scratch/noguard.txt diff shows exactly those five extra PAIR lines.

findings.claim: Wrapper policy: strict (identity wrappers only: memo, forwardRef, observer, Object.assign) gives antd 186/195 = 95.4%. Keeping today's any-call-with-identifier-first-argument unwrap (weekly.py:171, tests in test_weekly_review.py:83-87) adds one pair, Tour._InternalPanelDoNotUseOrYouWillBeFired = PurePanel, where PurePanel.tsx has 'export default withPureRenderTheme(PurePanel)'. That gives 186/194 = 95.9% and keeps every existing test. A risk of the any-call rule: genPurePanel(Dropdown, ...) would pair a PurePanel to Dropdown, and the merge shrinks the denominator. Recommended: keep the legacy unwrap and tag the pair kind 'wrapped' when the chain went through a non-identity call, so it is visible. Replay with the legacy flag labelled calendar and datepicker 'alias_of_external' (the chain ended at the imported dayjsGenerateConfig), so the cause needs a factory test before the external test.
findings.evidence: LEGACY=1 run: paired {default_export 32, named_export 2, static_member 1}, merged 14, reference 194.

findings.claim: shadcn is unchanged by the pairing rules: matches 1518/1573 before and after, with no pairs. Its 55 unmatched entries classify as object_member 34 (icons.tsx x19, mdx-components.tsx x15), alias_of_external 8 (chart Tooltip x4, Collection, I18nProvider, DirectionProvider, mdx Link), factory_result 5 (icon-*.tsx 'createIconLoader(...)'), member_alias 4 (ChartLegend = RechartsPrimitive.Legend), name_not_in_file 4 (ComboboxRoot x3, SelectRoot). These are Caliper gaps, so the 96.5% stays honest; the harness change should not touch it.
findings.evidence: scratch/run2.py shadcn v output.

findings.claim: Remaining antd unmatched after the change, 9 (strict): factory_result calendar, datepicker and Tour._InternalPanel (call results Caliper does not see), alias_of_external Form.List, Mentions.Option, TreeSelect.TreeNode (imported from rc-component), declared_not_reported QrcodeStatus (a plain 'export default function QRcodeStatus' that Caliper does not report; worth a Caliper-side look), key_collision InternalPanel, name_not_in_file RefIcon.
findings.evidence: scratch/run2.py antd v listing.

findings.claim: Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum cannot be replayed locally. Their unpaired counts in dl-new are 40, 50 and 25 of references 368, 664 and 1023. Chakra already merges 36 repeats by named_export, so it is the corpus where a wrong default or alias pairing would show most. Spectrum excludes 29 not_jsx entries, so the lowercase-default rule could meet more cases there; Mantine puts a displayName string such as '@mantine/core/Foo' on its components, which norm_name handles by taking the last segment.
findings.evidence: dl-new/weekly/weekly.json reference blocks. The corpora are not installed locally; the effect on them is inferred.

input.numbers: antd, replayed against the same RDT dump and a fresh Caliper rdt output built from origin/main 53970b80. Components matched: baseline 165/207 (79.7%). Strict 186/195 (95.4%). Legacy any-call 186/194 (95.9%). Strict plus the collision fix 187/195 (95.9%). Legacy plus the collision fix 187/194 (96.4%). Guards off, a negative control only: 188/192 (97.9%). Of the 42 baseline unmatched: 21 become matches, 5 merge into a counted component, 7 are excluded (6 not_jsx_default, 1 static_member), and 9 stay unmatched. shadcn: 1518/1573 before and after. Caliper's collapsed layers were not replayed.

proposed_branches.name: fix/weekly-pairing
proposed_branches.scope: Rewrite pairing in scripts/weekly.py. Extend export_source/default parsing: a statement reader, strip ' as T' / satisfies / '!', Object.assign and dotted wrappers (React.memo), and keep today's any-call-with-identifier-first-argument unwrap. Add local-alias resolution with displayName literals. Let pair() resolve the default export inside RDT's own file for entries whose name is the file's or directory's own name, and add a 'static_member' route for dotted names. Add the guards (own-name, same-file claim, name agreement, hop limit, no pairing into a collided key). Add a read cache. Add exclusions not_jsx_default and static_member. Do NOT exclude name_not_in_file entries.
proposed_branches.tests: New fixtures with exact expected pairings: (1) skeleton/Avatar.tsx 'const SkeletonAvatar...; export default SkeletonAvatar;' with RDT 'Avatar' and found {skeletonavatar} gives paired {'default_export':1}, keys [(f,'avatar'),(f,'skeletonavatar')], unpaired 0. (2) checkbox/Group.tsx 'export default CheckboxGroup as <T = any>(p: P) => JSX.Element;' and radio/group.tsx 'export default React.memo(RadioGroup);' each pair to their local Caliper name. (3) collapse/index.tsx 'import Collapse from "./Collapse"; export default Collapse;' with Collapse.tsx 'export default Object.assign(Collapse, { Panel });' and RDT 'Collapse' exact gives merged 1, reference 1. (4) dropdown index: 'import Internal from "./dropdown"; const Dropdown = Internal as typeof Internal & {...}; export default Dropdown;' pairs to (dropdown.tsx,'dropdown'). (5) image/Progress.tsx 'Progress.displayName = "ImageProgress"; export default Progress;' with found 'imageprogress' pairs. (6) Negatives, all asserting paired == {} and the stated cause: Form.tsx RDT 'List' with 'export default Form' and exact Form (cause alias_of_external); Mentions.Option when Mentions is unclaimed (own-name guard); 'const DatePicker = generatePicker<Dayjs>(cfg); export default DatePicker as T' with another Caliper component in the file (factory_result, no sole-component fallback); splitter InternalPanel into a claimed (file,'panel') (cause key_collision). (7) Exclusions: 'export default function confirm(c){}' with RDT 'confirm' is not_jsx_default, 'export default function Confirm(){}' with 'confirm' is not excluded; 'ConfigProvider.config = setGlobalConfig;' is static_member; 'Tour.Panel = PurePanel;' with 'import PurePanel from "./PurePanel"' is not excluded and pairs to the Caliper component in PurePanel.tsx. (8) Existing tests (wrapped default export, order-free merge, declaring-file pairing) still pass.
proposed_branches.cost_note: Python in the weekly script only. Runs once per corpus. File reads are per RDT entry that does not match exactly: at most ~100 per corpus, each follows up to 8 hops, and a read cache makes each file cost one read. The own-name lowercase check reads a file only when the name is lowercase or dotted. Caliper runtime and memory are untouched.
proposed_branches.expected_gain: antd components 79.7% to 95.4% (strict) or 95.9% (legacy); shadcn unchanged at 96.5%. Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum unknown until the CI run.

proposed_branches.name: feat/weekly-unmatched-record
proposed_branches.scope: weekly.json records why entries are unmatched or paired. stats['unmatched'] = {cause: count} (always present, sorted keys). stats['unmatched_list'] = [[file, name, cause, props]] sorted by props descending then file, capped at 40, plus 'unmatched_more' (count over the cap). stats['paired_list'] = [[file, name, kind, target_file, target_name]] for every non-exact pairing, capped at 60. stats['excluded_sample'] = {cause: up to 5 names}. stats['key_collisions'] = count and up to 5 keys. Add 'reference_version': 2 to each corpus entry, and make findings() skip the recall comparison (with a note) when versions differ. Add an 'Unmatched by cause' table to the markdown. Causes: alias_of_external, factory_result, member_alias, object_member, declared_not_reported, name_not_in_file, key_collision, sibling_only, not_detected. Test the record shape and the cap.
files: .github/workflows/weekly.yml (only if the artifact needs no change; none expected)
proposed_branches.tests: Unit test: 3 unmatched entries with causes alias_of_external, factory_result and key_collision give exact counts and list order; with 45 entries the list is capped at 40 and unmatched_more == 5; findings() returns no 'worse' note when reference_version differs.
proposed_branches.cost_note: Classification runs once per unmatched reference item (about 9 in antd, 51 in shadcn, 25 to 50 in the other corpora), a few regex searches on a file already in the read cache. Size: about 100 bytes per list row, so at most about 4 KB plus 6 KB per corpus, roughly 30 KB for five, against 8 KB today.
proposed_branches.expected_gain: Future analysis needs no re-run of RDT. A reviewer can see over-pairing from paired_list on the Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum runs.

proposed_branches.name: fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions
proposed_branches.scope: Optional, one component in antd (187 against 186). caliper_components and caliper_layer_members give repeated (file,name) keys a '#2' suffix in a shared helper, ordered by the entry's key so both calls agree. reference() assigns RDT entries to colliding keys by best Jaccard prop overlap before the exact and pairing steps. Without it the collision is only counted and left unmatched.
proposed_branches.tests: Fixture: Caliper keys (Panel.tsx,'panel') twice with prop sets of 12 and 9; RDT 'InternalPanel' (13, superset of the 12-set) and 'Panel' (the 9-set) assign 1:1, giving components [2,2]. Without a collision nothing changes.
proposed_branches.cost_note: Per collided key only; zero cost when no key repeats (1 key in antd, 0 in the other four measured or replayed; Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum unknown).
proposed_branches.expected_gain: +1 antd component, and it removes a silent last-wins prop comparison.

risks: Unseen corpora. The rules are validated only on antd and shadcn. Mantine (polymorphicFactory/factory with a displayName string and static 'Foo.extend'), Chakra (withContext/createRecipeContext wrappers; 36 named_export merges already) and Spectrum ('const _Foo = forwardRef(Foo); export {_Foo as Foo}', 29 not_jsx exclusions) may expose chain shapes or wrong pairs this replay could not. Mitigation: run the branch through the weekly workflow (workflow_dispatch), download weekly.json, and read paired_list and unmatched_list before merging. The raw RDT dumps are too large to upload (shadcn 75 MB), so the compact lists are the artifact.

Reference redefinition. Recall will jump (antd about +16 points) with no change in Caliper. The previous record uses the old reference, so findings() should compare reference_version and skip recall comparison when it differs, otherwise the next real drop would be masked or compared with the wrong baseline. docs/measurement.md must say the jump is the harness, and its 2026-10-31 table is already stale (81.3% on 203 against the 79.7% on 207 the run produced).

The any-call unwrap and a regex statement parser are heuristics: a HOC factory such as genPurePanel(Dropdown, ...) can pair an unrelated wrapper to Dropdown and shrink the denominator. The claim guard stops it only inside one file. Keep the 'wrapped' tag so these pairs are countable.

Excluding lowercase default exports (not_jsx_default) assumes such a function is never used as a component; a lowercase name can still be re-exported under a capital name. 0 of 7 new exclusions in antd and shadcn are components Caliper reports; check the excluded_sample on the other corpora.

proposed_branches.expected_gain: antd components 79.7% to 95.4% (strict) or 95.9% (legacy); shadcn unchanged at 96.5%. Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum unknown until the CI run.

files: .github/workflows/weekly.yml (only if the artifact needs no change; none expected)
proposed_branches.tests: Unit test: 3 unmatched entries with causes alias_of_external, factory_result and key_collision give exact counts and list order; with 45 entries the list is capped at 40 and unmatched_more == 5; findings() returns no 'worse' note when reference_version differs.

proposed_branches.name: fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions
proposed_branches.scope: Optional, one component in antd (187 against 186). caliper_components and caliper_layer_members give repeated (file,name) keys a '#2' suffix in a shared helper, ordered by the entry's key so both calls agree. reference() assigns RDT entries to colliding keys by best Jaccard prop overlap before the exact and pairing steps. Without it the collision is only counted and left unmatched.
proposed_branches.tests: Fixture: Caliper keys (Panel.tsx,'panel') twice with prop sets of 12 and 9; RDT 'InternalPanel' (13, superset of the 12-set) and 'Panel' (the 9-set) assign 1:1, giving components [2,2]. Without a collision nothing changes.
proposed_branches.cost_note: Per collided key only; zero cost when no key repeats (1 key in antd, 0 in the other four measured or replayed; Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum unknown).
proposed_branches.expected_gain: +1 antd component, and it removes a silent last-wins prop comparison.

risks: Unseen corpora. The rules are validated only on antd and shadcn. Mantine (polymorphicFactory/factory with a displayName string and static 'Foo.extend'), Chakra (withContext/createRecipeContext wrappers; 36 named_export merges already) and Spectrum ('const _Foo = forwardRef(Foo); export {_Foo as Foo}', 29 not_jsx exclusions) may expose chain shapes or wrong pairs this replay could not. Mitigation: run the branch through the weekly workflow (workflow_dispatch), download weekly.json, and read paired_list and unmatched_list before merging. The raw RDT dumps are too large to upload (shadcn 75 MB), so the compact lists are the artifact.

Reference redefinition. Recall will jump (antd about +16 points) with no change in Caliper. The previous record uses the old reference, so findings() should compare reference_version and skip recall comparison when it differs, otherwise the next real drop would be masked or compared with the wrong baseline. docs/measurement.md must say the jump is the harness, and its 2026-10-31 table is already stale (81.3% on 203 against the 79.7% on 207 the run produced).

The any-call unwrap and a regex statement parser are heuristics: a HOC factory such as genPurePanel(Dropdown, ...) can pair an unrelated wrapper to Dropdown and shrink the denominator. The claim guard stops it only inside one file. Keep the 'wrapped' tag so these pairs are countable.

Excluding lowercase default exports (not_jsx_default) assumes such a function is never used as a component; a lowercase name can still be re-exported under a capital name. 0 of 7 new exclusions in antd and shadcn are components Caliper reports; check the excluded_sample on the other corpora.

Excluded entries that are real components Caliper cannot see (factory results, external aliases) stay in the denominator on purpose; the recall number will not reach 100% and the unmatched record says why. Some of these (QrcodeStatus in antd) are Caliper gaps worth a separate fix.

proposed_branches.name: fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions
proposed_branches.scope: Optional, one component in antd (187 against 186). caliper_components and caliper_layer_members give repeated (file,name) keys a '#2' suffix in a shared helper, ordered by the entry's key so both calls agree. reference() assigns RDT entries to colliding keys by best Jaccard prop overlap before the exact and pairing steps. Without it the collision is only counted and left unmatched.

risks: Unseen corpora. The rules are validated only on antd and shadcn. Mantine (polymorphicFactory/factory with a displayName string and static 'Foo.extend'), Chakra (withContext/createRecipeContext wrappers; 36 named_export merges already) and Spectrum ('const _Foo = forwardRef(Foo); export {_Foo as Foo}', 29 not_jsx exclusions) may expose chain shapes or wrong pairs this replay could not. Mitigation: run the branch through the weekly workflow (workflow_dispatch), download weekly.json, and read paired_list and unmatched_list before merging. The raw RDT dumps are too large to upload (shadcn 75 MB), so the compact lists are the artifact.

Reference redefinition. Recall will jump (antd about +16 points) with no change in Caliper. The previous record uses the old reference, so findings() should compare reference_version and skip recall comparison when it differs, otherwise the next real drop would be masked or compared with the wrong baseline. docs/measurement.md must say the jump is the harness, and its 2026-10-31 table is already stale (81.3% on 203 against the 79.7% on 207 the run produced).

The any-call unwrap and a regex statement parser are heuristics: a HOC factory such as genPurePanel(Dropdown, ...) can pair an unrelated wrapper to Dropdown and shrink the denominator. The claim guard stops it only inside one file. Keep the 'wrapped' tag so these pairs are countable.

Excluding lowercase default exports (not_jsx_default) assumes such a function is never used as a component; a lowercase name can still be re-exported under a capital name. 0 of 7 new exclusions in antd and shadcn are components Caliper reports; check the excluded_sample on the other corpora.

Excluded entries that are real components Caliper cannot see (factory results, external aliases) stay in the denominator on purpose; the recall number will not reach 100% and the unmatched record says why. Some of these (QrcodeStatus in antd) are Caliper gaps worth a separate fix.
